change_summary: The paper has been withdrawn at the editor's request, and its full text and PDF were replaced by a withdrawal statement. The stated reason is that the indoor temperature records had been processed with an incorrect sensor calibration, so the reported results cannot be relied on. The stored paper's headline result, a 2.1 °C lower mean daily peak indoor temperature in green-roofed flats, is based on indoor temperature data.
evaluation: Your Section 2.2 cites Okafor et al. [14] as the source of the 2.1 °C green-roof cooling parameter in your model, and the stored paper reports that same 2.1 °C lower mean daily peak indoor temperature. Your Discussion says your green-roof result scales almost directly with the 2.1 °C taken from Okafor et al. [14]. The paper has been withdrawn, and the withdrawal statement says the indoor temperature records had been processed with an incorrect sensor calibration, so the reported results cannot be relied on. This touches both uses, and the impact on your draft is high because your key model parameter and your headline estimate depend on that figure.
recommendation: The paper has been withdrawn at the editor's request, and the withdrawal statement says the indoor temperature records had been processed with an incorrect sensor calibration, so the reported results cannot be relied on. Your Section 2.2 sets the green-roof cooling parameter to 2.1 °C citing Okafor et al. [14], and your Discussion says its green-roof result scales almost directly with the 2.1 °C reduction it takes from that paper. Because your model depends on this figure, raise it with your co-authors or supervisor before editing text, and find a replacement value and re-run the model. Then re-check the Discussion claims and update or remove reference [14], citing the withdrawal if you keep it.
